# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 19 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 19

**1** Jesus said: "Blessed is the one who came into being before coming into being.

**2** If you become my disciples and hear my words, these stones will minister to you.

**3** For you have five trees in Paradise that do not change in summer or winter, and their leaves do not fall.

**4** Whoever knows them will not taste death."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Came into being before coming into being"** — consensus. PNEUMA's "existed before existing" is a reasonable equivalent but loses the Coptic's specific *šōp* (come into being / become). The becoming-language matters: what has a before-becoming is prior to creation.

**"These stones will minister to you"** — consensus. The stones are the material world transformed into servants for the initiated.

**"Do not change"** — LOGOS preferred over PNEUMA's "never change." "Never" is an intensifier not in the Coptic.

**"Will not taste death"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "will never die." Third occurrence of the promise from Saying 1; consistent rendering reveals the structural echo.

**Synoptic Parallels:**
- No direct Synoptic parallel for v.1 (the pre-existent blessed one)
- "Stones will minister" — cf. Matt 4:3 / Luke 4:3 (stones becoming bread); here it is reversed: the disciple commands the stones
- Five trees in Paradise — no Synoptic parallel; this is esoteric tradition specific to Thomas and related texts

**Theological Note:** The three repetitions of "will not taste death" (Sayings 1, 18, 19) form a structural bracket. The promise of the prologue (Saying 1) is confirmed in the midst of the collection by returning to the same idiom. The reader is being reassured that the path described is working.
